name: MCEC Summer Camps (University of Maine)
operator_name: Maine College of Engineering and Computing, University of Maine
description_short: A set of STEM summer programs at the University of Maine for students aged about 7 to 18, covering robotics, electronics, 3D printing, coding and building computers. Some are day camps, some are residential (overnight), and several are free.

warnings: The page shows no year. Dates were taken to be summer 2026 because the page says 'The 2026 MSTI Program will not be held', and the weekdays match 2026 (for example, July 13 is a Monday). That season has already passed as of today (2026-10-13). No 2027 dates or prices are posted.

This is a hub page for many separate programs, not one camp. The programs differ in format (day, commuter or residential overnight), ages, prices and contacts. Because of that, camp_type and price_per_week are left blank.

The Build Your Own Computer, LEGO Builders and Programming in Minecraft camps point to USM STEM Outreach (https://usm.maine.edu/stem-outreach/stem-camps/). They may be run by the University of Southern Maine and held somewhere other than Orono.

The Maine Summer Transportation Institute (MSTI, grades 6-8, free, residential, July 6-10) was not held in 2026, so it is not listed as a session. The page says to watch for 2027 announcements next spring.

The listed address and phone are the Maine College of Engineering and Computing (MCEC) office, not necessarily where each camp meets. Several programs have their own contacts: bradley.denholm@maine.edu (AMC Robotics), sarah.glatter@maine.edu (Semiconductor), info@umaineppf.org (Chip Moody), amanda.collamore@maine.edu (MSTI).
The AMC Robotics Camp had a May 31 application deadline and 36 spots in total across its three sessions. This is a deadline, not a registration opening date.
The Chip Moody and SELF programs give grade levels rather than ages. SELF is described as for Maine high school students.
